title: #010. Production Line Setup & Mixed Production

# #010. Production Line Setup & Mixed Production

<!-- section:scenario -->
A factory operates $n$ candidate production lines $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Opening line $i$ (`open[i]` $\in \{0, 1\}$) incurs a fixed setup cost `fixedCosts[i]` and unlocks capacity up to `capacities[i]` units of continuous output (`quantities[i] >= 0`). If line $i$ remains closed (`open[i] = 0`), its output **must be `0`**.

Each unit produced on line $i$ earns contribution margin `margins[i]` and consumes `materialUsages[i]` units of shared raw material (available supply `materialCap`). Choose which lines to open and how much to produce on each open line to **maximize net profit**.

<!-- section:io -->
- **Input (`P010Input`)**: `margins: number[]`, `fixedCosts: number[]`, `capacities: number[]`, `materialUsages: number[]`, `materialCap: number`
- **Output (`P010Output`)**: `{ open: number[], quantities: number[], netProfit: number }`

<!-- section:example -->
In Case 1 (`margins = [50, 40, 35]`, `fixedCosts = [600, 300, 250]`, `capacities = [30, 40, 25]`, `materialUsages = [2, 1.5, 1]`, `materialCap = 70`):

- Line 0 has a high unit margin (`50`), yet earns only `25` per unit of scarce material (`50 / 2`) while carrying a steep `600` fixed setup cost.
- Leaving Line 0 **closed** (`open = [0, 1, 1]`) and producing `quantities = [0, 30, 25]` maximizes net profit at `(40*30 - 300) + (35*25 - 250) =` **`1,525`**!

<!-- section:hint1 -->
Both binary `open[i]` and continuous `quantities[i] >= 0` are declared in the starter code. Link them for every line $i$ with the linear inequality:
$$\text{quantities}[i] \le \text{capacities}[i] \cdot \text{open}[i]$$
When `open[i] = 0`, this forces `quantities[i] <= 0` -> `quantities[i] = 0`.

<!-- section:hint2 -->
Also enforce the shared material budget `dot(input.materialUsages, quantities) <= input.materialCap`, and maximize net profit `dot(input.margins, quantities) - dot(input.fixedCosts, open)`.

<!-- section:formulation -->
$$
\begin{aligned}
\max \quad & \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} m_i q_i - \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} F_i y_i \\
\text{s.t.} \quad & 0 \le q_i \le C_i y_i && \forall i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\} \\
& \sum_{i=0}^{n-1} a_i q_i \le M_{\text{cap}} \\
& y_i \in \{0, 1\} && \forall i
\end{aligned}
$$

This classic **binary-continuous capacity linking** pattern bridges Chapter 1's pure LP and pure binary models — and prepares you directly for fixed-charge networks and Big-M reformulations in Chapter 2!
